records.text: Pand Stonebinder is a First Aid trainer who teaches practical techniques. For further improvement, Pand points trainees to Doctor Gregory Victor at Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands.

Eyahn Eagletalon is preparing a headdress for her brother, who is soon to stand before Chief Bloodhoof. While tanning leather straps, she seeks Azure and Bronze Feathers to finish the design. She considers making the headdress and witnessing the ceremony her part in her brother's occasion.

Tal is Thunder Bluff's Wind Rider Master, arranging air travel and explaining that travel to the Crossroads depends on prior contact with its master, Devrak. He also carries leather goods there for Jahan Hawkwing. Tal warns against defiling sacred land and responds to threats by summoning an enraged wyvern.
Torn is a banker in the tauren settlement at Bloodhoof Village. His bank service gives visitors a place to store and retrieve their belongings.
Jyn Stonehoof is a weapons merchant at Bloodhoof Village. He sells weapons and has work to offer.
Karn Stonehoof is a blacksmithing trainer at Bloodhoof Village. His trade is the forge: he offers instruction in blacksmithing to those who seek the craft.
Taur Stonehoof supplies blacksmithing materials at Bloodhoof Village. He supports the village's smiths and apprentices with goods for their craft.
Brek Stonehoof is a mining trainer at Bloodhoof Village. He offers instruction in mining, teaching visitors the skills needed to work the earth.
Kurm Stonehoof supplies mining goods at Bloodhoof Village. His wares serve miners and others working with the earth.
Fyr Mistrunner is a bread vendor in Thunder Bluff.
Tepa trains tailors in Thunder Bluff. She delights in the beauty of sewing patterns, seeing each as a design with its own voice.
Mahu supplies leatherworkers and tailors in Thunder Bluff, supporting both crafts with trade goods.

Una is a master leatherworker and trainer in Thunder Bluff. She taught Jangdor, and takes pride in seeing that former student now teach one of his own. She respects his judgment and recognizes the skill he sees in his student, whose Wild Leather training she can complete. Her words also affirm the Horde’s pact with Thrall and its determination to hold its lands.
Mak is an apprentice leatherworker in Thunder Bluff. He hopes to finish crafting a fitting gift and then seek Cairne’s counsel, looking for wisdom from the tauren leader.

Bena Winterhoof trains alchemists in Thunder Bluff. Her response to seeing the undead was grief at their horror and loneliness; she says the Earth Mother urged her to save them. Her compassion gives her alchemy a personal purpose beyond instruction.
Mani Winterhoof sells alchemy supplies in Thunder Bluff.
Teg Dawnstrider learned enchanting young, continuing a family tradition he says has lasted for generations. He says his son is learning it now, carrying that practice into another generation.
Nata Dawnstrider sells enchanting supplies in Thunder Bluff.
Komin Winterhoof is an herbalism trainer in Thunder Bluff who greets visitors with an offer to teach herbalism.
Nida Winterhoof sells herbalism supplies in Thunder Bluff.

Kuna Thunderhorn is a bowyer who stocks fletching goods and offers goods to browse. His shop title and service flags also identify ammunition and repair services, making his trade broader than bow making alone.
Tand is a basket weaver in Thunder Bluff who also sells goods.
Nan Mistrunner is a fruit vendor in Thunder Bluff.
Hogor Thunderhoof is a guns merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Delgo Ragetotem is an axe merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Etu Ragetotem is a mace and staff merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Kard Ragetotem is a sword and dagger merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Sunn Ragetotem is a staff merchant who also offers repair services. His role is practical and specific: he supplies staves while serving customers with repair needs.
Sura Wildmane is a war harness vendor in Thunder Bluff who also repairs gear and has work to offer.
Tah Winterhoof is a humanoid found in Thunder Bluff.
Kaga Mistrunner is a meat vendor in Thunder Bluff and has work to offer.
Aska Mistrunner is a cooking trainer.
Naal Mistrunner sells cooking supplies. His stock supports cooks preparing food, giving him a specialized role among the local vendors.
Kah Mistrunner is a fishing trainer in Thunder Bluff.
Sewa Mistrunner sells fishing supplies in Thunder Bluff.
Siln Skychaser is a shaman trainer whose greeting invokes the spirits. The training dialogue offers instruction in their ways and information about dual specialization.
Tigor Skychaser is a shaman trainer in Thunder Bluff. He greets visitors as ones the spirits have guided to him and teaches the ways of the spirits.

Beram Skychaser is a shaman trainer who teaches the ways of the spirits. He greets visitors as guided to him by the spirits and offers training, including instruction on unlearning talents and dual specialization.

Turak Runetotem trains druids in Thunder Bluff and sees their path as service to nature: animals and plants are both friends and charges, and druids preserve balance. He urges students to keep their minds clear and hearts strong. His teaching invokes Cenarius and directs students toward the Cenarion Circle and Moonglade, whose knowledge and solace he values.
Sheal Runetotem is a druid trainer whose teaching invokes the many paths of the Earth Mother and the care of ancestors. Her training dialogue reflects a spiritual view of druid practice.
Kym Wildmane is a druid trainer whose teaching invokes the many paths of the Earth Mother and the care of ancestors.
Sheza Wildmane is a humanoid found in Thunder Bluff.
Kary Thunderhorn trains hunters and describes her teaching as grounded in the ways and traditions of the ancestors. She may also respond that she lacks the knowledge being sought.

Holt Thunderhorn is a hunter trainer closely associated with the Earthmother. A description of him calls him one of the most revered hunters and says he has bested powerful beasts; his own teaching stresses the connection between beasts, the Tauren, and all who inhabit Azeroth. He also teaches hunters to train and guide pets.
Urek Thunderhorn is a hunter trainer who asks whether a hunter prefers guns or bows. He may also say that he lacks the knowledge being sought.

Torm Ragetotem trains warriors and teaches that there is always more to learn. He believes a warrior’s honor survives death, directing learners to the Fallen Hero of the Horde. He also recommends testing their skill against peers on Fray Island under Klannoc Macleod and seeking Ruga Ragetotem’s trial.
Sark Ragetotem trains warriors, encouraging them to remember that there is always more to learn.
Ker Ragetotem trains warriors, encouraging them to remember that there is always more to learn.
Miles Welsh trains priests and offers goods for sale.

Malakai Cross trains priests and teaches that helping those in need is the way of the divine: the reason for giving aid matters more than the method. He directs learners to Ogtinc in Azshara to assist the Cenarion Circle.

Father Cobb trains priests and teaches that helping those in need is the way of the divine, with the reason for aid mattering more than the method. He refers learners to Ogtinc in Azshara to help the Cenarion Circle.
Archmage Shymm is an undead mage trainer. He greets fellow mages and cautions that magic will burn the untrained.
Ursyn Ghull is a mage trainer. His greeting welcomes fellow mages; his advice is to beware magic, which can burn the untrained. His training exchange is brief and practical.
Thurston Xane is an undead mage trainer who greets fellow mages and warns that magic will burn the untrained.

Veren Tallstrider works leather into clothing and armor for Thunder Bluff’s people. He trades leather goods for hides and supplies, and takes pride in young people who show interest in leatherworking. He greets aspiring hunters warmly and wishes them honor for their clan.

Cairne Bloodhoof is High Chieftain and welcomes Horde folk to Thunder Bluff. He expects service to his people, valuing tracking and hunting skill. He encourages interest in tauren history and lore, seeing remembrance of Winter Veil traditions as valuable despite the goblins' commercial motives. He urges respect for spirits of past and present.
An Honor Guard serving Thunder Bluff as part of the city’s defenses.
Bluffwatchers help visitors find civic services, including the bank, inn, guild master and wind rider master.
Tagain sells cloth armor.
Grod sells leather armor.
Fela sells heavy armor.

Apothecary Zamah serves the Royal Apothecary Society in Thunder Bluff, seeking Serpentbloom’s potential to advance the Forsaken and the Dark Lady’s cause. She feels sorrow for Stonetalon’s spirits despite her heart no longer beating. She prepares toxin for use against the Venture Company and urges allies not to avoid dark paths if they lead to victory, dismissing guilt over poisoning the company.

Melor Stonehoof is a hunter who treats the hunt as more than food or honor, using it to teach the Earthmother’s ways. He sends hunters into distant lands after dangerous beasts, including Steelsnap and Frostmaw, and teaches how to lure Frostmaw. His concern for Deadmire’s suffering gives that hunt a merciful purpose.
Pawe Mistrunner is a humanoid in Thunder Bluff who has tasks for travelers.

Sage Truthseeker advises Cairne, whom he trusts, while worrying that others in the political climate may be misleading the Elder Council about the Forsaken alliance. He seeks knowledge before advising the Chieftain. As a scholar, he studies the Platinum Discs and supports the continuing effort to uncover the truth about Uldum.

Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem offers counsel on tauren spiritual concerns. Stonetalon’s plight pains Magatha, who believes Forsaken knowledge of disease can help heal the land and strengthen trust between their peoples, and refers allies to Apothecary Zamah. Magatha enchants Incendia powder to summon Arikara, expressing fear that changed tauren lore has angered the creature and put Cairne Bloodhoof at risk. A partnership with Jediga also brings Magatha ancient lore, including Beth’Amara’s reputation for alchemy and metal transmutation.
Gorm Grimtotem is a Grimtotem of Thunder Bluff who offers work to visitors.
Cor Grimtotem is a Grimtotem of Thunder Bluff who offers work to visitors.

Auld Stonespire praises Cairne for uniting their people in Thunder Bluff but cannot forgive the foes who drove Auld’s people from their holy ancestral lands in the southern Barrens. Auld views that expulsion as deserving severe revenge and seeks Charlga Razorflank’s heart, hoping vengeance will bring peace at life’s end.

Zangen Stonehoof tends Thunder Bluff’s sacred flame and speaks of the Earth Mother, honored ancestors, and spiritual guidance. He is researching a centaur artifact in the Thousand Needles and asks for moonwell water, which he sends onward to his associate Rau Cliffrunner for use.

Mosarn is a respected Thunder Bluff blacksmith whose apprentices help produce arms and armor for tauren braves; the Grimtotems also favor his work. He recognizes the Blackened Iron Shield as one he made, but says his many commissions leave him unable to recall its individual history.
Krumn is Thunder Bluff’s guild master. He explains guild formation and offers guidance on organizing a guild, invoking the safety and honor that come from standing together.
Thrumn is a tabard vendor in Thunder Bluff who can replace a lost Blood Knight Tabard or Tabard of the Hand.

Clarice Foster is a grieving widow whose anger is sharpened by her husband Yuriv’s devotion to the Light and the crusade that kept him away from her and their children. After his death, she gives up his pendant and asks that it be placed on his tomb at the Sepulcher, wanting nothing more to do with him or the keepsake.
Kon Yelloweyes is a humanoid of Thunder Bluff who offers work to visitors.

Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem is a Cenarion Circle researcher who sends others to gather materials and help investigate threats to the natural world. His work ranges from studying Un’Goro’s soil and the mysterious morrowgrain to the tainted druids of Wailing Caverns. He acknowledges the danger of the research, and when a shard is delivered, it leaves him troubled: he warns that the Emerald Dream holds unsettling truths best left unspoken.

Nara Wildmane is a Thunder Bluff druid whose dreams are troubled by the Druids of the Fang. She wants their leaders stopped so the Barrens can escape their twisted vision for the land. She also works with Sage Truthseeker to investigate Uldum, though she admits they do not yet know what the sealed gates or miniature discs will reveal.

Xanis Flameweaver guides shaman through elemental studies, sending them onward to teachers of water and air. Xanis speaks with pride about a promising student's progress and recognizes that controlling air is difficult, while expressing confidence in their ability to meet its challenges.

Birgitte Cranston is a portal trainer in Thunder Bluff. She offers mages instruction in portal magic, describing portal conjuring as a skill available to a select group. Her training dialogue also turns away a character she judges not ready to grasp the subject.
Henen Ragetotem is a humanoid of Thunder Bluff who offers work to visitors.

Orm Stonehoof is respected for his skill as a maker of the brutal helm. He demands proof of worth: find the suffering chimaera matriarch in the Charred Vale and bring her galvanized horn. Once the trial is fulfilled, he makes the helm.

Innkeeper Pala welcomes guests to her Thunder Bluff inn. During Hallow’s End she invites visitors to dance for marzipan, and she helps feed the city’s New Year revelers by receiving celebration supplies. Her greetings also encourage guests to join the festivities.
Mooranta is a skinning trainer in Thunder Bluff.

Taim Ragetotem serves as an Alterac Valley battlemaster. His dialogue addresses prospective fighters and speaks of the valley's forces seeking victory, presenting him as a guide to the battleground's military service.
Chesmu is a banker in the settlement at Thunder Bluff. He offers the routine banking service to visitors.
Atepa is a banker in the settlement at Thunder Bluff. She offers the routine banking service to visitors.
Hewa is a cloth armor merchant who runs Hewa's Armory at the base of the wind rider tower in Thunder Bluff. She also has work to offer.

Ahanu is a leather goods merchant in Thunder Bluff who prepares goods for Jahan to sell at the Crossroads. His delivery quest sends the goods through Tal, the city's wind rider master, and he thanks the returning traveler for bringing hides from Jahan. He describes Jahan as his friend and frames the exchange as help between siblings.
Elki is a mail armor merchant at Thunder Bluff. Visitors can browse the goods he sells; his native role also includes repair service.
Chepi is a reagent merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Kuruk is a general-goods merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Shadi Mistrunner is a trade-supplies merchant in Thunder Bluff.
Pakwa is a bag vendor in Thunder Bluff.
Ohanko is a two-handed weapon merchant in Thunder Bluff who also repairs gear.
Halpa is a prairie dog vendor in Thunder Bluff.
Saern Priderunner greets visitors as friends and speaks of the Sun, wisdom, and the path ahead. He is associated with Plainsrunning instruction for Tauren.
Auctioneer Stampi is an auctioneer who offers visitors access to the Auction service.
Auctioneer Gullem is an auctioneer who offers visitors access to the Auction service.

Ghede oversees the receipt of Un'Goro soil for the Arch Druid's research and expects deliveries to be unloaded onto the piles. He speaks to visitors like a commanding officer addressing a private, and has little patience for unserious remarks or people he considers unprepared to serve the Cenarion Circle.

Bashana Runetotem coordinates the Cenarion Circle’s Morrowgrain research on Elder Rise. She supplies Tharlendris seed packets for cultivation with Un’Goro soil and accepts harvested Morrowgrain in groups of ten. She explains that producing the seeds is costly and that the Circle’s research continues while the herb’s mysteries remain unresolved.
Bulrug is a stable master who helps visitors stable their pets and recover lost companions.
Hesuwa Thunderhorn trains hunters to teach their pets. Her help is for hunters and their pets.
Thrag Stonehoof is an apprentice blacksmith who says he cannot hear the spirits Karn speaks of, despite listening for them.

Kergul Bloodaxe serves as a Warsong Gulch battlemaster for the Horde. He urges the defeat of the Silverwing Sentinels and addresses visitors preparing for the battleground, reflecting a clear allegiance to the Warsong cause.

Bluff Runner Windstrider greets heroes with news from both continents and beyond, and calls the able to the Ashenvale hunt, the Cenarion Circle's exploration of Kalimdor's frontiers, and the fight against the Scourge in the Plaguelands, sending them to other leaders for guidance.

Kray is an apprentice alchemist who worries that Bena is pushing herself too hard while making potions for their undead allies. He has seen her work day and night without enough sleep or food, and fears she may injure herself.
Vhan is an apprentice tailor who values making full use of hunted animals, saying that no part should go to waste. His brief remark connects his craft to the practical use of the hunt.

Mot Dawnstrider is an apprentice enchanter who longs to spend a fine day out on the open plains. He says his duty keeps him bound to his work, revealing a personal pull between that obligation and the freedom he wants.

Tarn is an apprentice leatherworker in Thunder Bluff who keeps a battle-worn axe close. He speaks with confidence about defending the tauren capital, recalling that enemy forces have entered it before and been driven back.

Rahauro serves Magatha and handles many of her tasks so she can attend to other matters. He is involved in her investigations of Ragefire Chasm, including the missing satchel of her clansman Maur Grimtotem and the threat posed by the troggs. He treats the trogg danger as a concern for the Horde and its orc members, while leaving Magatha's decisions to his mistress.
Ansekhwa is a weapon master who offers training in the weapons he has mastered. He also directs visitors seeking other weapon instruction to fellow weapon masters.
Martin Lindsey serves as an Arathi Basin battlemaster. He tells visitors who are not powerful enough that they cannot enter the battleground.
Nibbles is a prairie dog.
Whulwert Copperpinch sells Smokywood Pastures treats and farm goods for Winter Veil and urges visitors to greet Greatfather Winter.
Hunter Sagewind is a hunter of Thunder Bluff who ensnares foes with a Hooked Net and has work for adventurers.
Hunter Ragetotem is a hunter of Thunder Bluff who ensnares foes with a Hooked Net and has work for adventurers.
Hunter Thunderhorn is a hunter of Thunder Bluff who ensnares foes with a Hooked Net and has work for adventurers.

Rumstag Proudstrider is the Horde Cloth Quartermaster associated with Thunder Bluff's cloth drive. He asks for donations to replenish communal stores, explaining that community contributions support the tauren and earn Thunder Bluff's gratitude. His appeals cover several kinds of cloth and frame the effort as shared provisioning.

Elder Ezra Wheathoof is presented among several named elders whom visitors ask about. His greeting looks back on a time when his people hunted for glory and honor, then wonders whether life is so different now. He also invites questions about where to find Elder Windtotem.

Senior Sergeant Taiga recruits for the Horde's Ahn'Qiraj War preparations. She explains that official collectors are gathering supplies and directs prospective helpers to Warlord Gorchuk in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, identifying him as the person in charge.

A Thunder Bluff reveler welcomes the Lunar Festival with lively enthusiasm and admits not knowing how the fireworks work. Their festival greeting also describes moonlight that can take visitors to Thunder Bluff, while warning that old factional grudges still matter beyond the gathering.

Officer Thunderstrider handles commendation signets from adventurers, urging them to turn in ten at once for greater recognition while still accepting single signets. Their replies speak of recording deeds and acknowledging service, and offer continued help with further exchanges.

Lieutenant Lisande serves the Argent Dawn during the Scourge attack on Thunder Bluff. She urges defenders to fight the undead outside the city and investigate glowing runic circles she believes are significant, asking for proof of the Scourge slain and the investigation's results.

An Argent Dawn outfitter directs visitors to Light's Hope Chapel, where the order coordinates its opposition to the Scourge and provides instructions. The outfitter also offers visitors an option to spend runes.

The Festival Talespinner is a festival historian who keeps its past and documents the current year's celebrations. He says festival fires hold power and suspects sacred flames burn in enemy cities. He invites tales of the stolen city flames and responds to their return with interest.

Tauren commoners of Thunder Bluff enjoy the Midsummer Fire Festival and its fireworks, urge seeking out elders' wisdom at the Lunar Festival, and mention the druids of Nighthaven celebrating in Moonglade. They also tell, as mere legend, that Omen sleeps in Lake Elune'ara and appears once a year.
Althallen Brightblade is an Eye of the Storm battlemaster.
Fizim Blastwrench is an arena battlemaster for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. The shared greeting challenges aspirants to prove their ability and dismisses those judged unready as wasting time.
The Mulgore Pink Elekk is a hallucination of a pink elekk, seen only by those who are drunk or wearing Synthebrew Goggles, that unsettles customers at the beer gardens.
Poshken Hardbinder teaches inscription.
Mertle Murkpen sells inscription supplies.

A cheerful spirit visiting family and friends in Thunder Bluff during the Day of the Dead, he enjoys their stories and has a hearty appetite. He asks for more Bread of the Dead and offers a small holiday gift in return.

Aponi Brightmane is a warrior who was sent back from the Northrend front to recover from an infected arm wound. Frustrated by being unable to fight, she still wants to help her people and encourages hope. She is close enough to Tahu Sagewind to call him her brother and confide her restlessness to him.

Tahu Sagewind counsels Aponi Brightmane. While recovering away from the Northrend fighting, he urges her to be patient and spread hope, though he shares her concern that inaction may matter. He describes his people’s pursuit of balance and draws on teachings from Hamuul and the elves of Moonglade.

Dokin Farplain helps supply the Pilgrim’s Bounty feast. His requests concern dishes for the celebrants: he asks for candied sweet potatoes to be taken to Francis Eaton, and remarks that celebrants quickly go through the cranberry chutney brought to him.
Laha Farplain is a Pilgrim’s Bounty vendor in Thunder Bluff.

Mahara Goldwheat is a cooking trainer who notes that Pilgrim’s Bounty brings her many new students. The feast’s pie request is addressed to her at the tables outside Thunder Bluff, where she helps keep dishes stocked.

Krendle Bigpockets is the Orgrimmar Zeppelin Master at the Thunder Bluff dock. He announces the zeppelin and jokes that its test run crashed only once, despite the earlier concern about flying through the area.
Ruk Warstomper is a Battlemaster of Thunder Bluff.

Mosha Starhorn is a Horde Battlemaster whose greetings focus on battleground fighting. He asks whether a visitor is ready to fight for the Horde; another greeting tells an unseasoned visitor to return after gaining experience.
Deathscreamer Gura is an Isle of Conquest battlemaster who advises inexperienced volunteers to grow stronger before joining its battles.
A Ghostly Tauren Celebrant enjoys visiting friends and family again, celebrating and sharing old stories.
Magister Dalhyr is a Wintergrasp battle-mage who directs volunteers to join near the battle’s start and urges them to support the forces there once fighting begins.

The Public Relations Agent represents Crown Chemical Co. with an upbeat sales pitch, offering visitors a gift, a job, or something for themselves. They point customers to the company's mascot, Kwee, or the nearby Lovely Merchant when they need something the agent cannot provide.

Kwee Q. Peddlefeet presents themself as an official Crown Chemical Co. event mascot authorized to distribute Lovely Charm Collector’s Kits. Promoting the Charitable Charms program, Kwee encourages bracelets for friends, loved ones and admired leaders, or exchanges with Lovely Merchants for Love Tokens. For Cairne Bloodhoof, Kwee suggests a bracelet and expects the High Chieftain to be thrilled.
A junior investigator in the inquiry into the Crown Chemical Company. Steamwheedle seeks help with the investigation and points interested helpers to Detective Snap Snagglebolt in Orgrimmar.

place_records.text: You are in Thunder Bluff, Horde land in Mulgore on Kalimdor. Its main settlements are Elder Rise, Spirit Rise and Hunter Rise, and the city has a bank, an inn and a flight master. Prairie stalkers, flatland prowlers, prairie wolves and flatland cougars roam the land around it.

You are in Elder Rise, the part of Thunder Bluff where druids train and the Cenarion Circle works. Turak and Sheal Runetotem teach druids here, and Bashana Runetotem coordinates the morrowgrain research on the rise. Magatha Grimtotem's servant Rahauro investigates Ragefire Chasm, and Magatha regards the troggs that have come up from beneath Orgrimmar as a threat to the Horde. Flatland prowlers are about.

You are in Spirit Rise, a Horde settlement in Thunder Bluff where shamans and priests train. Siln, Tigor and Beram Skychaser teach shamans, and Malakai Cross teaches priests that aid matters most when it reaches those in need. Apothecary Zamah of the Royal Apothecary Society studies serpentbloom and grieves for the spirits of Stonetalon, which the Venture Company troubles. A windfury matriarch is about.

You are in Hunter Rise, the Horde part of Thunder Bluff where hunters and warriors train. Holt Thunderhorn teaches that beasts, tauren and the Earthmother are bound together, and Melor Stonehoof sends hunters after Steelsnap, a hyena roaming the Thousand Needles. Mosarn, a blacksmith, has apprentices who make arms and armor, and Fizim Blastwrench is an arena battlemaster for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit.

You are in The Pools of Vision, a Horde settlement in Thunder Bluff. Priest trainers Malakai Cross and Father Cobb teach that helping those in need is the way of the divine, and Birgitte Cranston teaches portal magic to a select few. Apothecary Zamah of the Royal Apothecary Society works here, and the area has its own vendors and trainers.
